thread:
Maya R.: getting pages — multiple jobs failing with CUDA OOMs and ECC errors on cluster-gpu-1. Customers seeing 503s for batch infer. stack traces point to sudden VRAM reclamation failures. paging oncall now.

oncall-bot: Incident detected: GPU ECC error spike on cluster-gpu-1. Paging @Jack T.. Severity: P2. Links: https://prometheus/alert/1765

Jack T.: oncall here, looking. which nodes? any pattern by model or instance type?

Maya R.: initial tail shows node gpu-node-12 and gpu-node-15. Both are a100-80G. Jobs were medium-batch transformer v2 (seq len 1024). Affected customers: 2 active long-running customers hitting dedicated pools; some hosted API requests falling back and timing out.

Sophie L.: I see increased ECC single-bit counts in last 10m and repeated kernel restart logs in kubelet on node 12. Also thermal spikes just before the errors.

Carlos G.: here's the quick nvidia-smi snapshot from node12:
```
Timestamp: 2026-03-15T11:33:02Z
+-----------------------------------------------------------------------------+
| NVIDIA-SMI 525.89.02    Driver Version: 525.89.02    CUDA Version: 12.1   |
| GPU  Name        Temp  Perf  Pwr:Usage/Cap| Memory-Usage | ECC Errors          |
| 12   A100-80G    86C    P0    310W/400W  | 65500MiB/81920MiB | single-bit: 42    |
+-----------------------------------------------------------------------------+
```
Kernel logs:
```
[11:32:58] NVRM: Xid (PCI:0000:65:00): 79, pid=0, GPU reported a ECC error
[11:33:00] kubelet: kubelet: Evicting pod due to OOM: container usage exceeds limit
```

Jack T.: ok. I'm going to cordon + drain node12 and node15, then set routing to dedicated capacity for the affected customers to reduce pressure. executing drain now.

Jack T.: run:
```
kubectl cordon gpu-node-12
kubectl drain gpu-node-12 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data --grace-period=60
```

deploy-bot: Started rollout to route traffic away from gpu-node-12 for customer-team-alpha. Change ID: r1234. (auto rollback on failure)

Maya R.: thanks. Sophie — can you capture Prometheus query for the recent ECC spike + thermal correlation? we need an alert change proposal after we stabilize.

Sophie L.: grabbing queries. current ECC alert is `sum(increase(nvidia_gpu_ecc_errors_total[5m])) > 0` -> noisy, pages on single-bit single events. recommendation: change to `sum(increase(nvidia_gpu_ecc_errors_total[5m])) > 3` AND fire only if also `avg_over_time(nvidia_gpu_temperature_celsius[5m]) > 80` for same host. that reduces noisy single-events while catching sustained failure.

Carlos G.: also seeing a VRAM fragmentation pattern: resident memory hits 95% briefly then OOM. We don't currently alert on fragmentation or short-lived resident spikes. propose: new alert `gpu_vram_resident_percent > 90 for 2m` and `gpu_free_memory_bytes < 5%` per node.

Jack T.: agreed. For immediate mitigation we routed affected jobs to dedicated capacity and restarted the nvidia driver on drained nodes. node12 reboot in progress, monitoring.

oncall-bot: Node gpu-node-12 marked unschedulable. Pod evictions: 12. Incident status updated. Paging silenced for 15m.

Maya R.: customer impact: two customers reported increased latency and ~40% request failure for ~8 minutes. We already contacted CS and created ticket CS-8421 to inform them. CS notified customers with an ops update.

Sophie L.: adding a short-term alert to reduce noise: change ECC alert -> severity: warning, do not page for warning; page only for critical (>=10 errors in 5m OR ECC errors + thermal >85C). I'll open a PR on monitoring.

Jack T.: after nodes come back we should run a targeted workload to reproduce and collect GPU metrics at higher resolution: enable 10s scrape for those nodes and record a 30m trace. Sophie, can you own the trace collection? Carlos will run repro jobs.

Sophie L.: will do. I'll create a dashboard with: per-node ECC counts, temperature timeseries, memory resident %, fragmentation estimate (nvml gpu_memory_pool fragmentation if available), and driver reset counts. panel suggestions:
- timeseries: ECC single/multi-bit (stacked)
- heatmap: per-GPU temperature over last 24h
- bar: resident % tail distribution (p95/p99)

Carlos G.: quick note — VRAM fragmentation metric isn't reported cleanly in our exporters. I'll add a small agent on nodes to sample `nvidia-smi --query-gpu=memory.used,memory.total --format=csv` and compute an approximation; push as `redwood_gpu_memory_fragmentation_percent` gauge.

Jack T.: good. We also should update the oncall runbook: current text says \"page on any ECC > 0\" which is too sensitive. Proposed change: \"ECC alert pages on sustained ECC errors or driver resets (>=10 errors in 5m OR >3 resets in 15m). Single-bit spike -> warning only.\" Maya, can you make the runbook PR?

Maya R.: yes, I'll draft runbook changes and link to the monitoring PR and dashboard. action items so far:
- Sophie: monitoring PR to change ECC thresholds + new VRAM resident alert (ETA 3h)
- Carlos: implement local agent to approximate fragmentation metric + push to prometheus (ETA 24h)
- Jack: follow up on node hardware health with SRE infra (firmware/BIOS) and open hardware ticket if ECC persists (ETA 6h)
- Maya: runbook + customer comms PR (ETA 2h)

Jack T.: current status: drained nodes, customers routed, reboot/driver restart in progress. no new pages for 7m. marking incident as mitigated for now but keep monitoring until next deploy cycle.

deploy-bot: Rollout r1234 succeeded. Traffic routed to dedicated pools for affected customers.

Sophie L.: quick dump of the alert change diff I'll PR (short):
```
- ALERT GPU_ECC_SPIKE IF sum(increase(nvidia_gpu_ecc_errors_total[5m])) > 0
+ ALERT GPU_ECC_SUSTAINED IF sum(increase(nvidia_gpu_ecc_errors_total[5m])) > 3
  FOR 5m
  LABELS { severity = \"warning\" }
+ ALERT GPU_ECC_CRITICAL IF sum(increase(nvidia_gpu_ecc_errors_total[5m])) > 10
  OR (sum(increase(nvidia_gpu_driver_resets_total[15m])) > 3)
  LABELS { severity = \"critical\" }
```

Maya R.: thanks. we'll also add an automated dashboard widget to surface nodes with both high temp and ECC errors so oncall can triage faster.

Carlos G.: one postmortem note: check airflow/HC provisioning in datacenter — thermal events clustered around 11:30 local. could be HVAC loop blip. I'll pull facility telemetry.

Jack T.: good catch. if facility telemetry shows HVAC blip we should file a joint incident with infra and facilities — avoids flipping nodes repeatedly.

Maya R.: summary for ops channel and exec: brief incident note + action items, will post once runbook + monitoring PRs are up. everyone add any missing items.

Sophie L.: adding test plan to PR: after changes deploy, run synthetic workload for 1h and ensure ECC alert fires only on real sustained events. will add unit tests for alert logic.

Jack T.: thanks team. I'll keep watch for 1h then sign off. if ECC starts again we escalate to hardware vendor.

Maya R.: closing thread for now. thanks all."
